svg.title: Why leaves and nodes are hashed differently
svg.desc: Without prefixes, a tree of four entries and a tree of two fake entries can share a root: each fake entry is the 64-byte concatenation of two child hashes, so hashing it as a leaf gives the same value as hashing the inner node. With 0x00 for leaves and 0x01 for nodes, the two computations can never coincide.

text.tspan: no prefixes: leaf = H(entry), node = H(left || right)
four real certificates a, b, c, d
two "entries" of 64 bytes each, never logged
H(x) = H(A || B): the fake leaf hashes exactly like the real inner node.
RFC 6962: leaf = H(0x00 || entry), node = H(0x01 || L || R).
a leaf hash and a node hash now start from different first bytes: they cannot be swapped.
